text: The Taliban has released a biography of its reclusive leader Mullah Mohammed Omar, asserting he is still alive and in charge. The 11-page document aims to dispel rumors of his death and reassert his jihadi leadership credentials. Omar's daily schedule is described, including delivering orders to jihadi commanders.

Hundreds attended Walter Scott's funeral in South Carolina, mourning the black US Coast Guard veteran fatally shot in the back by a white police officer. Scott's family and friends said his death would be a catalyst for change in America. Officer Michael Slager, who shot Scott, faces murder charges and potentially life in prison or the death penalty.

Former TSA agent Daniel Boykin sentenced to 6 months in jail for secretly videotaping female co-worker in bathroom. Boykin also broke into victim's home, taking videos and photos, and was found with over 90 videos and 1,500 images on his devices. He received 5.5 years' probation and GPS monitoring in addition to jail time.

Cape Verde is leveraging its rich musical heritage to boost its economy, with events like the Kriol Jazz Festival and the Atlantic Music Expo promoting local artists and attracting tourism. The country's creative sector is seen as a key driver of growth, with tourism expected to account for 20% of GDP by 2024. Government and private sector are collaborating to promote Cape Verde's music globally.

Arsenal beat Burnley 1-0, staying within four points of leaders Chelsea with a match between the two clubs next week. Chelsea have two games in hand, including a fixture against relegation-threatened QPR on Sunday. Arsenal's win was courtesy of a first-half Aaron Ramsey goal.

The original cast of Twin Peaks is backing David Lynch in his salary dispute with Showtime, releasing a video in support of the director as part of a #SaveTwinPeaks campaign. Lynch exited the revival project Sunday, citing insufficient funding. Showtime remains hopeful the project can continue with both Lynch and co-creator Mark Frost.

Andrew Getty, 47, heir to the Getty oil fortune, died of apparent natural causes at his home, with no foul play suspected. Getty had several health issues and an autopsy is to be conducted. His family has released a statement confirming his death and requesting privacy.

A Maryland court has delayed extraditing Nyia Parler, 41, to Philadelphia to face charges related to abandoning her quadriplegic son in woods, citing the need for her to complete an unspecified "treatment". Parler is accused of leaving her 21-year-old son in Philadelphia's Cobbs Creek Park for several days. She faces charges including aggravated assault and recklessly endangering another person.

NASA astrophysicist Amy Mainzer has named Asteroid 316201 after Malala Yousafzai, the Pakistani education activist and Nobel Peace Prize winner. The asteroid, discovered in 2010, orbits the sun between Mars and Jupiter every 5.5 years. Mainzer cited the underrepresentation of women among asteroid namesakes in choosing to honor Malala.

Gastrointestinal illness has affected 100 people on the Celebrity Infinity cruise ship. The CDC is investigating the cause, with two staffers set to meet the ship in San Diego on Monday. The vessel has a history of similar outbreaks, having been affected twice previously.

The entire "Star Wars" saga is being released on digital HD; "Vampire Diaries" star Nina Dobrev is leaving the CW series; and actor James Best, known for playing Rosco on "Dukes of Hazzard", has died.

Three US women arrested on terror charges: Keonna Thomas, 30, of Philadelphia, for attempting to join ISIS, and Noelle Velentzas, 28, and Asia Siddiqui, 31, of New York, for allegedly plotting domestic attacks. Thomas faces up to 15 years in prison.

HBO releases teaser for "True Detective" season 2, starring Colin Farrell, Vince Vaughn, Rachel McAdams, and Taylor Kitsch. The new season premieres June 21. The plot follows a murder investigation in California that exposes a web of conspiracy and betrayal.

A 32-year-old man, Carlos Colina, has been charged with assault and improper disposal of a body after human remains were found in a duffel bag in Cambridge, Massachusetts. The victim, identified as 26-year-old Jonathan Camilien, was known to Colina. Colina was arraigned on Monday.

Top college-bound basketball recruit Trey Moses asks high school freshman Ellie Meredith, who has Down syndrome, to prom, ditching his girlfriend. Moses made the invitation in Ellie's P.E. class with flowers and a poster referencing her favorite singer, Taylor Swift. The unusual prom-posal has gone viral on social media.

NBC debuts "A.D. The Bible Continues", a 12-part miniseries sequel to "The Bible", on Sunday at 9 p.m. ET. The show follows the early days of Christianity after Jesus' resurrection. It stars Juan Pablo Di Pace as Jesus.

Indiana Governor Mike Pence faces backlash for signing a religious freedom law that could allow discrimination against gays and lesbians. The move has boosted Pence's standing among ultraconservatives, potentially shifting the Republican presidential field further right. Similar "religious freedom" bills are being considered in at least 14 other states.

Apple releases new emojis with diverse skin tones and representations, including LGBTQ+ couples and a Palestinian flag. The update has sparked both praise and criticism, with some conservatives objecting to the new emojis. Other groups, such as redheads and Armenians, feel left out by the new additions.

Avril Lavigne reveals she was bedridden for five months with Lyme disease, which she believes she contracted from a tick bite last spring. The singer is now "80 percent better" and releasing a new single this month. She recuperated at her Ontario home with the help of her husband and mother.

New research suggests Anne Frank and her sister Margot died at least a month earlier than previously thought, likely in February 1945, due to a typhus outbreak at Bergen-Belsen concentration camp. The exact dates of their deaths remain unclear. Researchers re-examined archives and survivor testimonies to reach the conclusion.

Two Alabama college students, Ryan Calhoun and Delonte Martistee, have been arrested and charged with gang raping a woman at Panama City Beach during spring break. The suspects, students at Troy University, were identified after a video of the alleged assault was discovered during an unrelated investigation. They are due to make their first court appearance on Saturday.

A stray dog in Washington State survived being hit by a car, beaten with a hammer, and buried, before being found and taken to a vet for treatment. The dog, named Theia, is undergoing care for multiple injuries at a veterinary hospital. A fundraising campaign has raised over $10,000 to support her medical treatment.

The FBI has confirmed that Malaysian bomb maker Zulkifli bin Hir, also known as Marwan, was killed in a botched Philippine raid in January. Marwan was a wanted terrorist linked to Jemaah Islamiyah and Abu Sayyaf. The raid resulted in the deaths of 44 Philippine police commandos.

US Rep. Mike Rogers says Obama administration's emerging nuclear deal with Iran is flawed, giving Tehran billions in sanctions relief while allowing it to maintain nuclear infrastructure. The deal lacks tough safeguards to prevent cheating and its strictest restrictions expire in 10 years. Critics warn it could enable Iran to develop nuclear weapons.

"Mad Men" returns Sunday to conclude its run, likely picking up where it left off in July 1969, amid the Manson murders, Woodstock, and other pivotal events of the late 1960s. The final season is expected to explore the disintegration of the ad agency and its characters. Key characters, including Roger Sterling and Peggy Olson, may be poised for significant developments.

Giraffe Katie gives birth live on Animal Planet after hour-long labor at Dallas Zoo. The newborn, around 6 feet tall, was seen moving its ears and attempting to stand and nurse. The zoo described Katie as a champ for handling the ordeal under the spotlight of 10 cameras.

Loretta Lynch's confirmation as attorney general has been delayed a record six months, sparking concerns over racial bias. Senate Republicans deny the delay is due to Lynch's African-American background, citing partisan battles over issues like human trafficking and immigration. Lynch's nomination remains pending.

Three people were killed and five wounded in an attack on the attorney general's office in northern Afghanistan. Afghan security forces are engaged in an ongoing exchange of fire with the assailants. The office has been stormed in Balkh province.

Bob Barker returned to hosting "The Price Is Right" on April 1 for the first time in eight years, handling the "Lucky Seven" game at age 91 before handing over to Drew Carey. Barker appeared spry and didn't miss a beat. He hosted the show for 35 years before stepping down in 2007.

B.B. King hospitalized for dehydration caused by Type II diabetes, but released from hospital and resting at home. The 89-year-old blues legend was "much better" and spending time with grandchildren. King had previously canceled tour dates last year due to dehydration and exhaustion.

Dzhokhar Tsarnaev was found guilty on all counts in the Boston Marathon bombing. The verdict highlights the need to understand radicalization among young Muslims. Radicalism can be countered by showing that violence harms rather than helps Muslim communities.

CNN highlights top videos of the week, including a tour of Mike Tyson's abandoned Ohio mansion and an interview with a Bikram yoga student's allegations of sexual assault by founder Bikram Choudhury. Other top clips feature the Fury 325 rollercoaster and a shepherd's eyewitness account of the Germanwings crash.

The Pentagon has released a map showing coalition forces have retaken 25-30% of Iraqi territory seized by ISIS, with gains in central and northern areas. Experts say the map indicates a conventional push against ISIS front lines, rather than a more effective maneuverist warfare approach. ISIS is likely to continue asymmetric attacks to distract from its losses and maintain its image.

A 22-year-old soccer player was allegedly choked by a fellow passenger on an Air Canada flight from Toronto to Atlanta. The suspect was restrained by other passengers and met by US authorities upon landing. The suspect was taken for medical evaluation by Atlanta police.

A court hearing in the case of Rurik Jutting, a 29-year-old Briton accused of murdering two Indonesian women in Hong Kong, was adjourned until May. Jutting, a former Bank of America Merrill Lynch trader, was charged with murdering the women, whose bodies were found in his apartment in November. The case has been delayed pending analysis of forensic and DNA evidence.

A massive tornado tore through rural Illinois on Thursday, killing one person in Fairdale and causing widespread damage in several towns, including Rochelle and Kirkland. The twister cut a 22-mile path through Ogle County, destroying homes and businesses. Multiple tornadoes were reported across the Midwest, with eight touching down in Oklahoma, Kansas, and Missouri on Wednesday.

Don McLean's original manuscript for "American Pie" sold for $1.2 million at a Christie's auction. The 16-page draft includes lyrics and notes not used in the final version. The sale is the third-highest price for an American literary manuscript.

UNRWA chief Pierre Krähenbühl visits Yarmouk Palestinian refugee camp in Syria on Saturday to assess humanitarian situation. The camp, controlled by armed groups, has been besieged since 2012 and is home to 18,000 Palestinians and Syrians. Fighting has caused widespread malnutrition and medical shortages.

Saudi-led coalition airstrikes on Yemen's capital Sanaa have killed hundreds and left 16 million without electricity, with many more feared dead or displaced. Fighting between Houthi rebels and government forces has intensified, with over 600 killed in a week. The International Committee of the Red Cross has called for a humanitarian ceasefire to deliver aid.

Former Australia cricket captain and broadcaster Richie Benaud has died at 84. Benaud was a legendary leg-spinner and commentator revered globally for his wit and insight. Tributes have poured in from cricketing figures and leaders including Australian Prime Minister Tony Abbott.

A total lunar eclipse occurred early morning, visible in western North America and parts of South America, India, China, and Russia. The four-minute, 43-second eclipse was the shortest of the century. Visibility was limited on the East Coast due to sunrise.

Millionaire real estate heir Robert Durst has been charged with unlawful possession of a firearm after a .38 caliber revolver was found in his hotel room. Durst, 71, faces up to 10 years in prison if convicted. He is also awaiting extradition to Los Angeles to face a first-degree murder charge.

"Furious 7" is released Friday, four months after its Los Angeles premiere, with a tribute to late star Paul Walker. The film's producers rewrote the script and used special effects to finish Walker's scenes after his death in a car crash in November 2013. Co-star Vin Diesel gave a tearful speech at the premiere, saying the movie is "more than a movie".

Model Manuela Arbelaez accidentally revealed the price of a Hyundai Sonata on "The Price Is Right", winning a contestant the car. Host Drew Carey reacted with laughter, while Arbelaez was left mortified. The show has had a busy week, with former host Bob Barker making a guest appearance on Wednesday.

Thai Smile airline has unveiled an Airbus A320 with an "Adventure Time" theme, featuring characters from the Cartoon Network show. The plane's interior also features the show's characters. The inaugural flight is set to take place on April 4 from Bangkok to Phuket.

Baby ducks and their mother caused a commotion on a Washington street, prompting pedestrians to stop traffic and corral them to safety. The group was eventually escorted to a nearby grassy area. Pedestrians even surrendered an umbrella to help guide the mother duck.

Investigators have completed collecting main evidence from the Germanwings Flight 9525 crash site in the French Alps. A private security firm will guard the site until remaining debris is removed. The crash, which killed 150 people, is believed to have been caused by co-pilot Andreas Lubitz deliberately crashing the plane.

Cuba attends Summit of the Americas for first time since 1962, amid clashes between government supporters and dissidents. US and Cuba to discuss re-establishing formal relations, with US considering removing Cuba from terrorism sponsor list. Obama and Castro may interact on sidelines despite no scheduled meeting.

Jesus and his disciples likely supported themselves through a combination of begging, hospitality, and donations from supporters, including wealthy women such as Mary Magdalene and Joanna. The Gospel of Luke notes that some women Jesus had healed provided for him and his followers out of their resources. Wealthy individuals, including Joseph of Arimathea and Nicodemus, may have also contributed to Jesus' ministry.

California utility regulator orders PG&E to pay $1.6 billion penalty for unsafe gas pipeline operation, including $850 million for safety infrastructure improvements. The penalty stems from a 2010 pipeline rupture that killed eight people in San Bruno. PG&E has paid over $500 million in claims to victims and their families.

Lauren Hill, a 19-year-old basketball player who inspired millions with her fight against brain cancer, has died. Hill had played in a college game last year after the NCAA accommodated her wish to take the court. She raised $1.4 million for pediatric cancer research and was hailed as a "worldwide inspiration".

A massive fire broke out at General Electric's Appliance Park in Louisville, Kentucky, on Friday morning, sending thick smoke into the area. No injuries or entrapments were reported. The cause of the blaze, which reached at least four alarms, was unknown.

Iranian Foreign Minister Mohammad Javad Zarif has played a key role in nuclear talks with US Secretary of State John Kerry. Zarif, who has been described as "polished" and "jovial", has a lesser-known history that includes education in the US and involvement in the Iranian Revolution. He has spent more time with Kerry than any other foreign minister.

A Connecticut teenager with Hodgkin lymphoma remains in state custody after a court denied her request to return home. The 17-year-old is in remission after forced chemotherapy. Her attorney says she will remain in the hospital until treatment is complete, expected by late April.

Researchers at the University of Texas used computer software to analyze the language of "Double Falsehood" and found it was likely written by Shakespeare and John Fletcher, not 18th-century playwright Lewis Theobald. The study concluded Shakespeare wrote the play's first half, with Fletcher co-writing the second half. The findings were published in the journal Psychological Science.

French prosecutor Brice Robin denied knowledge of any video footage from Germanwings Flight 9525, contradicting reports by Bild and Paris Match that a cell phone video showed the plane's final moments. The Marseille prosecutor urged anyone with such footage to come forward. Investigators continue to probe co-pilot Andreas Lubitz's mental state, revealing he had a history of depression.

A US-born veteran from American Samoa is suing for citizenship, arguing the 14th Amendment guarantees it, despite the federal government denying his claim. The case, before the D.C. Circuit, could decide the citizenship status of American Samoans. A ruling is expected soon.

Blue Bell Creameries has temporarily shut down its Broken Arrow, Oklahoma, plant due to listeria contamination in a serving of ice cream. The company has recalled certain products made at the plant and is investigating the cause of contamination. The move comes amid a listeria outbreak linked to the company's products that has infected five people and caused three deaths in Kansas.

Al-Shabaab militants have attacked Garissa University College in eastern Kenya, killing and taking hostages. The attack is part of the group's escalating activities in the region. The assault is linked to broader instability in East Africa driven by radicalism, poverty, and poor governance.

US complains to Russia after Russian fighter jet intercepts US reconnaissance plane over Baltic Sea in "unsafe and unprofessional manner". The incident occurred in international airspace north of Poland. US and Russia exchanged conflicting accounts of the encounter.

A hooded angel with black wings, created by local artist Phillip Hyman, has become an icon of the Black Lives Matter movement after appearing near the site where Walter Scott was fatally shot by police in North Charleston, South Carolina. The artwork was used in protests outside City Hall. Hyman created the piece as a tribute to Scott and a statement on police brutality.

North Charleston police officer Michael Slager has been fired and charged with murder after a bystander's video showed him shooting unarmed black man Walter Scott eight times as he ran away. Slager initially claimed Scott took his Taser during a struggle. The witness who recorded the video contradicted Slager's account, saying Scott never grabbed the Taser.

ISIS claims to have launched an assault on Iraq's Baiji oil refinery, posting images of fighters inside the facility, but Iraqi security officials deny the group's claim of control. The refinery has been a key battleground in the past. Iraqi forces remain in control, officials say.

Nashville's district attorney has banned prosecutors from offering female sterilization in plea deals after it was revealed that the option had been offered four times in the past five years. The practice of offering sterilization as part of a plea deal is not unique to Tennessee and has been used in other jurisdictions, mostly for male defendants. The move has sparked debate about the constitutionality and morality of such deals.

Ebola cases continue to decline, with 30 new confirmed infections reported in the week of April 5. While Liberia and Sierra Leone show significant progress, Guinea remains a concern with unknown transmission chains. WHO reports improving surveillance but warns of potential new infections.

The NCAA has told a court it has no legal responsibility to ensure the quality of education for student-athletes, contradicting its long-held public stance that education is paramount. The organization is responding to a lawsuit from former University of North Carolina athletes who claim they didn't receive a real education due to an academic fraud scandal. The NCAA likened its role to that of a professional accreditation body, saying it is not liable for the actions of its member institutions.

Six people injured in explosion and fire at chemical plant in China's Fujian province. The blast occurred at an oil storage facility after a leak, with over 600 firefighters battling the blaze. The fire is now under control.

US police officer Michael Slager faces possible life imprisonment after video showed him fatally shooting Walter Scott in the back. The author argues that police body cameras could prevent such tragedies and increase accountability. Body cameras have been shown to reduce use-of-force incidents and complaints against officers.

US President Obama and Cuban leader Castro met at the Summit of the Americas, but tensions flared over Venezuela, with Maduro accusing the US of plotting against him. The US sanctioned Venezuelan officials, prompting Maduro to rally regional support against the move. Cuba's foreign minister publicly backed Maduro, creating a diplomatic "triangle of tension" at the summit.

A nuclear submarine in dry dock at Russia's Zvyozdochka shipyard has caught fire during repairs, with insulation igniting during welding work. The submarine, which has had its nuclear fuel unloaded, is not carrying ammunition and no one was injured. The fire is not considered a threat to personnel or the shipyard.

Tropical storm Maysak, also known as Chedeng, is approaching the Philippines, prompting warnings of flash floods and landslides. The storm is expected to make landfall on Sunday and authorities have taken precautionary measures, including evacuations and banning outdoor activities. Maysak's winds are currently sustained at over 70 mph.

NFL legend Deion Sanders publicly chastised his son Deion Sanders Jr. on Twitter for boasting about eating "hood doughnuts". Sanders Sr. reminded his son of his privileged upbringing, referencing his trust fund and luxury lifestyle. Sanders Jr. retweeted his father's rebuke.

Guatemala has one of the world's highest rates of femicide, with two women killed daily, amid a culture of impunity and machismo. The country's 36-year civil war legacy and lack of education and resources exacerbate the issue. Efforts by NGOs and some government initiatives offer hope for change.

Indian city of Malegaon requires cattle owners to register their livestock with police, including a photograph and description of unique features. The move aims to enforce a state-wide ban on beef sale and consumption. Over 100 owners have complied so far.

Indian police in Lucknow are deploying pepper-spraying drones to control unruly crowds. The drones, costing $9,560-$19,300 each, have been tested and are set to be launched officially later this month. The move has sparked concerns over freedom of speech and the use of authoritarian methods.

Christie's auction house sold Don McLean's handwritten manuscript of "American Pie" lyrics for $1.2 million. The 16-page manuscript was bought by an unnamed buyer. The song, released in 1971, is considered a timeless classic and a cultural anthem.

Thieves raided a safety deposit facility in London's Hatton Garden jewelry district over the Easter weekend, cracking open dozens of boxes in a daring heist reminiscent of a 1971 bank robbery. Police are investigating the sophisticated crime, looking for signs of inside involvement and scrutinizing security footage and forensic evidence. The gang is believed to have planned the raid meticulously, exploiting weaknesses in the target's physical and operational security.

7-Eleven is hosting "Bring-Your-Own-Cup Slurpee Day" on Saturday, allowing customers to fill their own cups for $1.49. Participating stores will have size limits and sanitation requirements. The promotion kicks off peak Slurpee season.

Kentucky Senator Rand Paul announced his presidential bid, despite a record of questioning landmark civil rights legislation and opposing key minority community issues. Paul's campaign message of "inclusion" was met with skepticism by critics, who cited his history of opposing the Civil Rights Act and Voting Rights Act. Paul's views were deemed "outdated" and "disqualifying" for a national leader.

A Lamborghini crashed into a guardrail at Walt Disney World Speedway on Sunday, killing 36-year-old passenger Gary Terry. The driver, 24-year-old Tavon Watson, was hospitalized with minor injuries. The incident occurred during the Exotic Driving Experience track event.

Aaron Hernandez's defense team wrapped up its case in under a day after prosecutors presented 131 witnesses over several months; the jury will now consider largely circumstantial evidence. Hernandez, 25, is accused of killing semi-pro football player Odin Lloyd in 2013. Closing arguments are set for Tuesday.

Chinese authorities have detained five women's rights activists, including Wu Rongrong, for "creating disturbances" after they planned to protest against sexual harassment on International Women's Day. Their fate will be decided by April 13, when they must be either released or formally arrested. The detentions come as China prepares to mark the 20th anniversary of the Fourth World Conference on Women.

Martin O'Malley says Hillary Clinton's perceived inevitability as Democratic presidential nominee is not unbreakable, citing her 2008 loss to Barack Obama. O'Malley, a possible contender, suggests the party needs a "robust conversation" about issues and challenges. He teases a potential presidential run without directly attacking Clinton.

Aaron Hernandez was sentenced to life in prison for the murder of Odin Lloyd. Lloyd's family members delivered emotional statements in court, praising his character and recalling fond memories. Hernandez was convicted of first-degree murder.

Ted Cruz courted Iowa's evangelical voters on a two-day campaign swing, using his faith to connect with the state's vocal Christian right. Cruz, the only official GOP contender, drew large crowds and emphasized social issues, including defending Indiana's religious freedom law. He aims to energize evangelicals, a key bloc in Iowa's Republican primary.

Marvel Studios releases new poster for "Avengers: Age of Ultron" featuring Paul Bettany as the Vision. New images also emerge for "Daredevil", "X-Men: Apocalypse", and "Fantastic Four" characters. Superhero movie promotions intensify ahead of summer releases.

Italian Coast Guard rescues 978 migrants in Mediterranean Sea off Libya's coast. Migrant deaths in the Mediterranean have surged to at least 480 this year. Most migrants come from West Africa, Somalia, and Syria via Libya.

TV5Monde, a French-language global TV network, regained control of one of its 11 channels after a cyberattack crippled its broadcasts and social media accounts. The network's websites and social media outlets displayed ISIS logos and markings, but there was no immediate claim of responsibility. The outage affected 260 million homes worldwide.

David Lynch will no longer direct the 2016 revival of "Twin Peaks" due to a funding dispute with Showtime Network. Lynch announced his departure via Twitter, citing insufficient budget to produce the show to his standards. Showtime expressed "saddened" by Lynch's decision, but vowed to continue with the project.

Jury deliberations begin in Boston bombing suspect Dzhokhar Tsarnaev's trial, while closing arguments are set in former NFL star Aaron Hernandez's murder trial. Sen. Rand Paul announces his presidential bid, and Chicago voters head to the polls in a mayoral runoff. Elections are also held in Ferguson, Missouri, amid ongoing controversy over the city's representation.

Tornadoes reported in Kansas and Missouri as severe storms swept through the region Wednesday night. Multiple sightings were reported, including near Goddard, Kansas, and Potosi, Missouri, where wind damage and flooding were also reported. More storms expected in the Midwest and surrounding areas on Thursday.

Jodi Arias sentenced to life in prison without parole for 2008 murder of ex-boyfriend Travis Alexander. Judge Sherry Stephens handed down sentence after Arias expressed remorse for her actions. Arias was found guilty of first-degree murder in 2013.

A Delaware family fell ill at a luxury villa in the US Virgin Islands, with the EPA finding preliminary evidence of the toxic pesticide methyl bromide at the site. The family was hospitalized after staying at the villa from March 14-22. The EPA is investigating a possible link to a fumigation at the resort on March 18.

Rolling Stone's article on a University of Virginia gang rape was deemed "deeply flawed" by a Columbia Journalism School review. The magazine's managing editor apologized for the story's fallout. Phi Kappa Psi fraternity may pursue legal action for defamation.

FBI agents and task force officers chased a suspect in Georgia on Saturday, resulting in a crash that injured two agents and a gunshot wound to the suspect. The suspect, 36-year-old Kevone Charleston, is accused of 32 commercial robberies dating to 2013. Charleston's injuries are not life-threatening.

Alaska Airlines Flight 448 made an emergency landing after a ramp agent was discovered in the cargo hold, where he had apparently fallen asleep. The plane had taken off from Seattle-Tacoma International Airport bound for Los Angeles. The employee was taken to hospital as a precaution before being discharged.

A North Carolina judge has ruled that Craig Hicks, accused of killing three Muslim students, is eligible for the death penalty. Hicks is charged with three counts of first-degree murder in the February shooting deaths of his neighbors. The case may be investigated as a hate crime.

Amnesty International report calls for Afghan authorities to protect women's rights activists from attacks by Taliban, warlords, and government officials. Women activists face rising violence, with 20% increase in women's killings in 2013, often linked to domestic violence and cultural traditions. Activists continue to push for change despite threats and violence.

A New York judge has allowed a wife to serve divorce papers on her husband via Facebook private messaging. The decision is part of a growing trend towards online service of process. The method was chosen due to the husband's efforts to evade traditional service.

Rev. Robert Schuller, US televangelist and founder of "Hour of Power", died at 88. Schuller, who founded Crystal Cathedral megachurch, had been diagnosed with esophageal cancer in 2013. His ministry faced financial troubles and a succession scandal in later years.

Four workers died and 45 were injured in a fire on Mexico's Abkatun Permanente oil rig off the Gulf of Mexico coast. The blaze was extinguished by Wednesday night after a massive evacuation and firefighting effort. Pemex denied reports of a platform collapse or oil spill.

Kansas has become the first US state to ban "dismemberment abortion", a procedure commonly used in the second trimester. The law, signed by Gov. Sam Brownback, allows exceptions to protect the mother's life or health. Opponents have vowed to challenge the measure in court.

Chinese TV host Bi Fujian sparks controversy after being caught on camera cursing late Chairman Mao Zedong at a dinner party. Bi later apologized for his "grave social consequences." CCTV says it will investigate the incident.

University of Kentucky guard Andrew Harrison apologizes for using a racial slur under his breath about Wisconsin's Frank Kaminsky after Saturday's loss. Harrison said the comment was "in jest" and later called Kaminsky to apologize. Kaminsky said he is "over it" after the two spoke.
"Arrested Development" will return for a fifth season, executive producer Brian Grazer said on a podcast. The new season will have 17 episodes. Netflix has not confirmed the report.

The Large Hadron Collider has resumed operation after a two-year shutdown, with particle beams circulating in its 17-mile ring. The experiment aims to recreate conditions after the Big Bang and uncover the universe's evolution. Scientists will now increase the energy of the beams to new record levels.

Iranian military aircraft flew within 50 yards of a US Navy helicopter over the Persian Gulf, sparking concern of a potential incident. The US military believes the maneuver may have been locally ordered. The US is considering a demarche protest against Iran.

Dzhokhar Tsarnaev found guilty on all 30 counts in Boston Marathon bombing trial. The jury will now decide whether to impose the death penalty in a penalty phase. Tsarnaev faces 17 capital charges, making him eligible for execution.

Four employees of Indian clothing chain FabIndia arrested for voyeurism after security camera found pointing at store changing room. Minister Smriti Irani spotted camera during store visit. Staff face up to three years in jail if convicted.

Iran's Deputy Sports Minister says the ban on women attending men's sports events will be lifted for some matches next year. The relaxation of rules will apply to indoor events, but not all sports. The move comes after international pressure, including from FIFA President Sepp Blatter.

Indian software pioneer Ramalinga Raju sentenced to 7 years in jail and fined $804,000 for role in $1.6 billion Satyam Computers Services fraud. Raju and 9 others convicted of cheating, conspiracy and breach of trust. Sentence handed down by special court following Central Bureau of Investigation probe.

Woman with cancer removed from Alaska Airlines flight in Hawaii after disclosing health issue to staff; airline later apologized and refunded tickets. Alaska Airlines cited concerns for passenger's well-being in decision to remove her. Passenger eventually rebooked and reached destination late Tuesday.

Turkish singer-songwriter Kayahan died of cancer at 66. He had been diagnosed with the disease multiple times since 1990. Prime Minister Ahmet Davutoglu tweeted condolences for the loss of a musician who contributed to Turkish music.

Israeli PM Benjamin Netanyahu criticised the Iran nuclear deal, saying it leaves Iran's nuclear infrastructure intact. US Energy Secretary Ernest Moniz defended the deal, saying it blocks Iran's pathways to a nuclear bomb. Democrats and Republicans continue to spar over the framework, with some GOP contenders saying a future president could negotiate a better deal.

Multiple shootings in Washington DC and Maryland were linked to a domestic kidnapping incident, authorities said. A guard at the US Census Bureau headquarters was critically wounded and a police chase ensued, ending in a shootout that injured an officer and the suspect. The kidnapping victim was found safe.

US soldier Chelsea Manning has joined Twitter, with tweets dictated to a communications firm due to her lack of internet access in prison. Manning is serving a 35-year sentence for leaking classified documents to WikiLeaks. She has gained over 26,000 followers since joining the platform.

US rapper Nelly arrested on drug charges in Tennessee after state trooper stops his private bus on I-40. Nelly charged with felony possession, simple marijuana possession and paraphernalia possession. Bus search also turns up handguns and suspected drug packaging.

A Delaware family fell ill after renting a villa in the US Virgin Islands, with the father in stable condition and two sons in critical condition; the EPA says exposure to the pesticide methyl bromide may be the cause. The EPA is investigating a possible link to a fumigation at the resort. A criminal investigation has been initiated.

Governments in Asia are cracking down on online dissent, jailing bloggers and journalists for criticizing authorities. Countries such as Singapore, Malaysia, China, and Vietnam are using laws and imprisonment to silence online voices. In Bangladesh, bloggers have been hacked to death with impunity for writing on sensitive topics.

Nina Dobrev is leaving "The Vampire Diaries" at the end of the current season. Fans expressed disappointment and anger on social media, citing concerns over the show's future without Dobrev's character. Producer Julie Plec supported Dobrev's decision, saying the show will continue with the Salvatore Brothers storyline.

ISIS fighters stormed Syria's Yarmouk Palestinian refugee camp on April 1, sparking intense fighting and a government bombing campaign that has worsened living conditions for the 18,000 remaining residents. The area has been besieged by pro-government forces since 2012, with aid groups struggling to deliver assistance. Civilians face dire shortages of food, water, and medicine amid the ongoing conflict.

NASA scientists discussed the search for extraterrestrial life, with estimates suggesting 40 billion Earth-like planets exist in the Milky Way. Upcoming missions, including the James Webb Space Telescope, will search for signs of life on exoplanets. The likelihood of communicating with intelligent life is low due to the brief duration of Earth's "Communication Age".

A 32-year-old Massachusetts man, Carlos Colina, is to be arraigned on murder charges on April 14 in connection with the discovery of a 26-year-old man's remains in a duffel bag in Cambridge. Colina was previously charged with assault and battery and improper disposal of a body. The victim, Jonathan Camilien, was identified on Monday.

Kanye West has settled a lawsuit with paparazzo Daniel Ramos, whom he assaulted at LAX in 2013. The settlement includes an apology from West, and the two have shaken hands. The case was set to go to trial next week before being dismissed.

US President Barack Obama's push for a nuclear deal with Iran has been driven by political considerations, weakening America's negotiating hand. The framework agreement announced this week allows Iran to maintain much of its nuclear infrastructure, sparking concerns among regional allies. Critics say the deal is a "win for Iran" and may embolden its regional ambitions.

US police fatally shoot hundreds of people annually, but the lack of comprehensive data collection hinders understanding of the issue. A 1994 law requires the Justice Department to gather data on police-related deaths, but it has not been enforced. Activists and the Obama administration are calling for mandatory data collection to shed light on the problem.

Five Americans exposed to Ebola in Sierra Leone have been released from a Nebraska hospital after three weeks of monitoring. The clinicians, who work for a Boston-based aid group, did not develop the virus. A sixth healthcare worker remains hospitalized in Maryland in fair condition.

Mark Ronson's "Uptown Funk!" extends its record reign on the Billboard Hot 100 chart to 13 weeks. The song has also reached the top 10 list of longest-running No. 1 singles in Hot 100 history. Newcomer Natalie La Rose's "Somebody" featuring Jeremih debuts in the top 10.

April 8 marked "Rex Manning Day" for fans of the 1995 film "Empire Records". Other film-inspired dates include April 14, tied to "Titanic", and October 3, known as "Mean Girls Day". Other notable dates are April 25 and October 21, 2015, referenced in "Miss Congeniality" and "Back to the Future Part II".

"Grace of Monaco" starring Nicole Kidman will premiere on Lifetime on May 25 after being pulled from US theatrical release. The Weinstein Co. sold the film directly to Lifetime following poor international box office. The critically-panned film opened last year's Cannes Film Festival.

Tokyo's Shibuya ward has passed an ordinance allowing same-sex couples to register for "partnership certificates", granting them limited rights such as hospital visitation and co-signing tenancy agreements. The move is seen as a step towards marriage equality in socially conservative Japan. Neighboring wards are considering following Shibuya's lead.

California's ongoing drought is impacting national food prices, with past increases in fruits and vegetables, and expected rises in beef and veal prices this year. The drought's effects are also being felt beyond California, with other Western states experiencing extreme drought conditions. Food price increases are expected to continue, although the extent of the impact remains uncertain.

University of Michigan to screen "American Sniper" despite student objections, citing commitment to freedom of expression. Over 200 students had petitioned against the film's showing. Alternative screening of "Paddington" to be offered.

The 2015 MTV Movie Awards featured a mix of hits and misses, with highlights including Amy Schumer's opening monologue and Channing Tatum's impromptu twerking for Jennifer Lopez. Performances by Fall Out Boy and Charli XCX were also praised. The ceremony was marred by a few misfires, including Schumer's archery fail and some awkward jokes.

A 20-30ft section of fiberglass boat, suspected to be debris from Japan's 2011 tsunami, was towed into an Oregon harbour. The wreckage contained yellowtail jack fish, a species native to Japanese waters. The fish will be taken to the Oregon Coast Aquarium for further study.

Nigeria marks one year since Boko Haram kidnapped nearly 300 schoolgirls, with President-elect Muhammadu Buhari pledging to combat the militant group. Most of the girls remain missing, with fears they were raped, brutalized, and enslaved. The #BringBackOurGirls campaign continues to trend on Twitter.

The Easter Triduum, comprising Good Friday, Holy Saturday, and Easter Sunday, is a Christian observance that reflects the human experience of suffering, transition, and transformation. The three days symbolize the crucifixion, a period of darkness and uncertainty, and the resurrection, representing a shift from suffering to hope. The Triduum's themes are echoed in everyday life, as people experience personal struggles and transformations.

Kenya has frozen 86 bank accounts linked to suspected Al-Shabaab supporters following a university massacre that killed 147 people. The government is tracking the finances of suspected militants and has a list of suspects across the country. Kenya has also launched airstrikes against Al-Shabaab training camps in Somalia.

Entrepreneur Jia Jiang releases book "Rejection Proof" after completing "100 Days of Rejection" project, in which he deliberately sought out rejection to overcome his fear. Jiang's project went viral and led to speaking engagements and job offers. He shares tips on turning rejection into opportunity in his book.

US Attorney General Eric Holder reminds Justice Department personnel that soliciting prostitution is prohibited, regardless of local laws. The directive comes after a report found DEA agents engaged in misconduct with prostitutes abroad. Employees caught with prostitutes face suspension or firing, Holder says.

A white suspect, Kenneth Stancil, has been arrested for fatally shooting a white colleague, Ron Lane, at North Carolina's Wayne Community College on Monday. Authorities are investigating the killing as a possible hate crime. Stancil was arrested in Florida on Tuesday after fleeing the scene.

Amnesty International reports a rise in death sentences and executions worldwide in 2014, driven by governments' knee-jerk reactions to terrorism and crime. Despite this, the number of executions recorded globally dropped to 607, and 140 countries have now abolished the death penalty in law or practice. Executions were recorded in 22 countries last year.

A Duke University student has admitted to hanging a noose from a tree near the student union, prompting protests and a university investigation. The student is no longer on campus and faces disciplinary review. Criminal investigations are ongoing.

Richard Dysart, Emmy-winning actor known for his role as Leland McKenzie on "L.A. Law," has died at 86 after a long illness. Dysart appeared in every episode of the series and won an Emmy in 1992. He had a diverse career in film and TV, with roles in "That Championship Season," "The Hospital," and "Being There."

Easter's date varies annually due to its tie to lunar cycles and the vernal equinox. The holiday's timing is linked to Passover, and its calculation differs between Western and Eastern Orthodox Christians, resulting in sometimes separate celebration dates. A recent "blood moon" lunar eclipse coincided with Good Friday and Passover due to the shared lunar basis of the holidays.

Comedian Chris Rock tweets about being stopped by police three times in seven weeks, sparking debate over racial profiling. Rock's posts draw support and criticism, with some urging him to take steps to avoid being pulled over. Actor Isaiah Washington suggests Rock "adapt" by changing his vehicle to avoid profiling.

Lynyrd Skynyrd's original drummer, Robert Lewis Burns Jr., died in a solo car crash in Cartersville, Georgia, on Friday night at age 64. Burns was not wearing a seatbelt at the time of the crash. He was a founding member of the band in 1965, but left before their 1975 album "Nuthin Fancy".

A photo of a cat on stairs has sparked online debate over whether it's going up or down, with the image going viral on social media. The picture was uploaded to Imgur and shared on 9gag.com. Advertisers are capitalizing on the online buzz.

US and its partners reached a framework nuclear deal with Iran, limiting its nuclear program and blocking its ability to build a nuclear weapon. Opponents are expected to push back, citing dubious assumptions and assertions. The deal includes a rigorous inspection regime and Iran's ratification of the Additional Protocol.

University of Virginia is under investigation for handling of sexual assault cases, having never expelled a student for the offense despite 183 expulsions for honor-code violations since 1998. The US Department of Education is conducting a Title IX investigation into UVA. The school has instituted a zero-tolerance policy on sexual assault following a now-retracted Rolling Stone article.

Indiana Pacers player Chris Copeland was stabbed outside a New York nightclub, and two Atlanta Hawks players, Pero Antic and Thabo Sefolosha, were arrested on obstruction charges after interfering with police at the scene. Copeland is in stable condition with knife wounds to his elbow and abdomen. The suspect, a 22-year-old Brooklyn man, is in custody pending charges.

Twisted Sister to embark on farewell tour "Forty and F*ck It" in 2016, marking band's 40th anniversary. Tour will feature new drummer Mike Portnoy, replacing late A.J. Pero. Band to perform two shows in Pero's honor.

John Travolta dismisses HBO's new Scientology documentary "Going Clear" without having seen it, citing his 40 years of positive experience with the church. Travolta credits Scientology with helping him cope with his son's death in 2009. The actor is promoting his new film "The Forger" in Clearwater, Florida, a city with ties to Scientology.

"Furious 7" breaks box office record with $146 million haul, with fans praising the film's emotional tribute to late star Paul Walker. The movie's ending, featuring a montage of Walker scenes set to "See You Again", left many viewers tearful. Fans widely praised the tribute as sincere and fitting.

"Game of Thrones" Season 5 premieres Sunday in a record 170 countries, with story arcs converging and battles intensifying as the show approaches its midpoint. Expect key character interactions, including Tyrion and Daenerys, and rising tensions among common folk. The season will diverge from George Martin's source books.

Four individuals were recently rescued after being stranded at sea for extended periods, with survival times ranging from 12 days to over a year. The survivors, including a sailor, a fisherman, a teenager, and a tsunami survivor, used various methods to stay alive, such as rationing water and eating raw fish. All four were eventually rescued, with some being spotted by passing ships or found by rescue teams.

The first six "Star Wars" films will be available on digital HD on Friday, accompanied by special features. The bonus content includes behind-the-scenes looks, including a focus on the sound effects. Sound designer Ben Burtt explains the origins of the Geonosians' insect-like sounds.

A US jury has found Dzhokhar Tsarnaev guilty on all 30 counts related to the 2013 Boston Marathon bombings. Survivors and victims' families expressed a mix of emotions, from relief to gratitude, over the verdict. Tsarnaev's sentencing is pending.

China's former security czar Zhou Yongkang has been formally charged with bribery, abuse of power, and leaking state secrets. Zhou, a former member of the Communist Party's top decision-making body, is the highest-ranking official to face corruption charges. His case will be tried in Tianjin.

A 21-year-old quadriplegic man with cerebral palsy was abandoned by his mother in a Philadelphia park, where he was found after four days with severe dehydration and other health issues. His mother was arrested in Maryland and faces multiple charges, including aggravated assault and neglect. She allegedly left him in the park to visit her boyfriend.

Walmart's opposition to Arkansas' religious freedom law resonated with other business leaders, prompting Gov. Asa Hutchinson to vow to revise the bill. The company's stance reflects a growing trend of corporate support for gay rights and nondiscrimination policies. Some Republicans, including former Gov. Tim Pawlenty, are urging the party to take note of the shift.

A lapsed Catholic writer recounts how Pope Francis' inclusive and compassionate approach rekindled their faith. The Pope's tone and actions, such as welcoming LGBTQ+ individuals, have resonated with many former Catholics. Cardinal Gerald Lacroix attributes the Pope's impact to his inner freedom and devotion to the Gospel.

Mary Kay Letourneau Fualaau and her husband Vili Fualaau, who had a sexual relationship when she was his teacher and he was 13, are set to give an interview to ABC's "20/20". The couple, who married in 2005, will discuss their marriage and plans to lift her sex offender status. They are celebrating 10 years of marriage this month.

Hillary Clinton's presidential bid makes her a barometer for US gender equality. Her win or loss will be scrutinized for its implications on women's representation in politics. The outcome will be influenced more by partisanship and the economy than sexism.

Amnesty International reports a 22% decline in global executions in 2014, but a 28% rise in death sentences, with governments using the death penalty to combat terrorism and instability. At least 607 people were executed worldwide in 2014, excluding China. The number of people on death row globally is estimated to be at least 19,094.

Japan's Defense Minister says the country's Air Self Defense Force has never encountered an extraterrestrial UFO. The claim was made in response to a query from lawmaker Antonio Inoki, who has previously claimed to have seen a UFO. Inoki's question was raised during a Upper House Budget Committee meeting.

Mark Wahlberg to star in "Patriots' Day", a film about the Boston Marathon bombing, playing retired Commissioner Ed Davis. The film is being produced by CBS Films and will feature research from CBS News' "60 Minutes". A rival film, "Boston Strong", is also in the works at Fox.

Democratic presidential hopefuls Martin O'Malley and Jim Webb appeared at separate events in Iowa, showcasing their differing styles as they vie for the nomination. O'Malley worked the room at a Des Moines dinner, while Webb was more subdued, later appearing more at home at a veterans event. Both face long odds against frontrunner Hillary Clinton.

Nine British citizens, including four children, were arrested in Turkey on Wednesday for attempting to cross into Syria illegally. The group held British passports and included three men and two women accompanying the children. The Turkish military did not disclose their suspected motives.

The US Department of Justice has charged FedEx with 15 counts, including conspiracy and money laundering, for allegedly transporting prescription pharmaceuticals dispensed with illegal prescriptions. FedEx denies the charges, arguing it is a common carrier exempt from liability for possessing contraband. The case raises questions about corporate liability and the government's strategy to target the supply chain of the illegal drug market.

Kenyans mourned 147 victims of last week's Garissa University College terrorist attack, sharing their stories on social media using #147notjustanumber. The attack, claimed by Al-Shabaab, killed mostly Christian students after gunmen separated them from Muslims. Easter church services were held under armed guard, with congregations paying tribute to the victims.

Swedish photographer Johan Bavman documents fathers taking advantage of the country's generous parental leave policy, which grants 480 days of leave to be shared between parents. Despite incentives to encourage equal sharing, only 12% of couples divide the leave equally. Bavman's project aims to showcase the experiences of fathers who take extended leave.

US President Barack Obama reaffirms commitment to maintaining Israel's military edge over Iran amid criticism from Israeli PM Benjamin Netanyahu over Iran nuclear deal. Obama says he is "absolutely committed" to ensuring Israel's security. Talks on final draft of deal to continue until June 30.

US Religious Freedom Restoration Act, enacted in 1993, has spawned 20 state-level laws, sparking controversy over alleged use as pretext for anti-gay discrimination. Cases under the laws have mostly benefited religious minorities, not Christian denominations. Notable cases include a Native American's right to wear eagle feathers and a Brazilian faith's use of a sacramental tea containing a hallucinogen.

Five Chinese feminists face up to 5 years in prison for campaigning for gender equality, after police recommended charges of "disturbing public order". The women were detained before International Women's Day on March 8. Prosecutors are set to decide on formal charges by Monday.

Selena's family is creating a hologram-like figure of the late singer using new technology. The digital embodiment, called "Selena the One", will sing, dance and release new music. The project is set to launch in 2018 with a tour and collaborations with current artists.

Michele Bachmann compares President Obama to Germanwings co-pilot Andreas Lubitz, saying both "flew their nation into the rocks". Bachmann's comment sparked outrage on her Facebook page. The remark comes amid tense Iran nuclear deal negotiations.

Ryan Gosling's directorial debut "Lost River" has been released theatrically after premiering at Cannes last year, with the film's gritty portrayal of decaying Detroit sparking both criticism and praise. Gosling says the city's crumbling landscape was the inspiration for the film, which he began shooting before writing the script. The film's release is limited to select theaters in the US and UK on April 10.

A 19-year-old British man, Yahya Rashid, has been charged with terror offenses after being detained at Luton airport upon returning from Turkey. Rashid faces charges of preparing and assisting terrorism. He is due to appear in court.

Vince Neil's rendition of the US national anthem at a Las Vegas Arena Football League game was widely panned, echoing past controversies surrounding performances by artists like Roseanne Barr, Jimi Hendrix, and Michael Bolton. Neil's version was deemed a "butchering" of the song. Several other celebrities have faced criticism or acclaim for their anthem performances.

Almost 2,000 WWI soldiers' graffiti inscriptions have been discovered in an underground city near Naours, France. The writings, dating back to 1916, include names and hometowns of Australian, British, and American soldiers. The site, rediscovered after changing hands in 2013, is being documented by photographer Jeff Gusky.

Palestinian Authority becomes 123rd member of International Criminal Court, granting jurisdiction over alleged crimes in Palestinian territories since 2014. Israel and US opposed move, warning it could hinder peace talks. ICC may investigate war crimes on both sides, including those committed during last summer's Gaza conflict.

Anthony Ray Hinton, 58, was released from prison after nearly 30 years on death row in Alabama for murders he maintained he did not commit. A judge ordered his release after the state moved to dismiss charges. Hinton was wrongly convicted in the 1985 killings of two Birmingham-area fast-food managers.

Most Americans receive tax refunds, averaging $3000, and can file taxes simply and for free, creating a "happy ending" that overshadows the complexity and unfairness of the US tax system. Tax preparation services capitalize on this by offering add-on services to grateful taxpayers. The simplicity of tax filing has transformed Tax Day into a spending spree.

Jordan Spieth remains atop the Masters leaderboard after a steady third round, holding a four-shot lead over Justin Rose. Phil Mickelson and Rory McIlroy also posted strong rounds, but couldn't close the gap. Spieth will look to win on Sunday, needing to avoid a collapse to hold off the chasing pack.

A woman has pleaded not guilty to charges of falsifying a marriage license application as part of an immigration scam, having married 10 times between 1999 and 2010. She is accused of marrying multiple men to help them gain permanent residence status. If convicted, she faces up to four years in prison.

Indiana pizzeria Memories Pizza sparks controversy after owners say they won't cater same-sex weddings, prompting boycotts and harassment threats, but also a $842,000 outpouring of support. The restaurant's stance is tied to the state's new Religious Freedom Restoration Act. Police investigate threats against the business.

Mindy Kaling's brother Vijay Chokalingam posed as black to apply to medical school, claiming it showed affirmative action's "unfair advantage". He was accepted to one lower-ranked school, contradicting his claim of special privilege. Chokalingam now plans to write a book about his experience.

Antarctica's Esperanza Base recorded a temperature of 63.5°F on March 24, potentially the highest ever recorded on the continent. The World Meteorological Organization is investigating the reading's validity. A committee of experts will review the data and make an official determination by late summer or early fall.

US officials say plans to retake Mosul from ISIS this spring are on hold, with no timeframe set for the operation. Iraqi forces and allies are making progress against the group, but officials stress that taking Mosul will be a complex and time-consuming effort. Airstrikes have targeted ISIS positions around the city.

Irish betting firm Paddy Power sparks outrage with tweet likening Newcastle's losses to "Kop beatings" to deaths of unarmed African-American men. The company later deletes the tweet and claims it was a joke. The incident draws widespread condemnation on social media.

Nyia Parler, 41, has been charged with attempted murder and other counts after leaving her quadriplegic son in woods for days. Parler is being held in Maryland for treatment before extradition to Philadelphia. The 21-year-old man was found dehydrated and malnourished with a cut on his back.

Kim Ki-Jong, accused of stabbing US Ambassador Mark Lippert in Seoul, has been charged with attempted murder and other counts. The attack occurred during an event on March 5, with Lippert suffering an 80-stitch wound. Kim's trial is expected to begin within 14 days.

Jill Dillard, daughter of "19 Kids and Counting" stars Jim Bob and Michelle Duggar, has given birth to a son named Israel David. The baby, weighing 9 pounds 10 ounces, was born after his due date. Dillard, a student midwife, had prepared for a potentially late arrival.

"Furious 7" is projected to debut at $135-$138 million in North America and near $300 million worldwide this weekend. The film is playing in 4,003 US theaters and over 10,500 screens internationally. It is on track to post the largest three-day opening since November 2013.

US Secret Service supervisor Xavier Morales has been placed on administrative leave after a female employee accused him of making unwanted sexual advances and attempting to kiss her. Morales' security clearance was suspended following the incident at a party on March 31. The agency is facing another scandal amid ongoing efforts to recover from a series of high-profile missteps.

Hillary Clinton is set to announce her 2016 presidential bid, bringing extensive experience but also facing challenges including doubts over her authenticity and concerns from Democrats about her liberal credentials. Clinton must connect with voters and articulate a compelling vision to overcome these hurdles. She will also face scrutiny over her husband's influence and potential conflicts of interest.

The US Department of Justice is set to begin negotiations with Ferguson, Missouri, to reform its police department, which was found to have engaged in racially discriminatory practices. The city has also seen significant changes, including the election of two new black city council members and the resignation of the police chief and city manager. The scope of the changes will depend on the influence of local activists and residents on the DOJ negotiations.

US woman's 2-year-old cat Felix goes missing at JFK Airport after Etihad Airways flight from Abu Dhabi; airline says it's investigating and working to locate the cat. The cat's carrier was damaged during transit, allowing it to escape. Etihad is reviewing its pet handling procedures.

US sailor Louis Jordan, 37, rescued at sea after 66 days adrift following storm that capsized his boat. Jordan survived by collecting rainwater and catching fish attracted to his laundry. He was found in good physical condition by the crew of a container ship off Norfolk, Virginia.
